panel_arrangement: CPU and GPU rows by three grid columns
strip_geometry_basis: Two-bar strips retain the requested fixed canvas and type size. Text and worker labels receive explicit bounds checks.
caption_text: The top row uses a ceiling of 248 physical CPU cores, and the bottom row uses one GPU device. Each column identifies the same interior grid on the two platforms. Orange bars show the hand-tuned baseline and blue bars show ESM.md. Each point equals useful updates divided by median elapsed seconds from twelve matched runs. Useful updates are the interior-cell count multiplied by the total number of complete steps. Thin lines span the observed minimum and maximum individual rates for each implementation, rather than confidence intervals. Each facet has its own zero-based linear rate axis, with a common stated unit. Required boundary, overlap, gathering and coordination work remains inside the recorded solver time. Redundant tile work does not add to useful updates. Active worker counts are retained separately from the configured CPU budget. Unrounded rates, all twelve raw timing pairs and the exact timer scope remain in the data. Within each grid, both routes use the same selected actual worker team. Team sizes and nonempty spatial owners are recorded separately from the ceiling. Actual CPU worker-team counts are printed inside the poster CPU bars.
observed_range_definition: minimum and maximum of twelve individual useful-update rates
